picks.title: Elvis Presley Rightsholders Sue Anthropic for Training on 274 Songs Without Permission
picks.rationale: New lawsuit: the Presley rightsholders, a plaintiff not seen before in this section, sue Anthropic over training on 274 named songs. It adds a major catalog owner to the AI-training litigation front.
picks.excerpt: The owners of Elvis Presley's music have sued AI company Anthropic, accusing it of training its models on 274 Presley songs without permission.

picks.title: Making a track with DEATHPIXIE and Suno | In The Cut
picks.rationale: New Suno showcase: a studio writing camp builds tracks for the virtual rapper Death Pixie, showing a team songwriting workflow around Suno that producers can copy.
picks.excerpt: Suno visits Glenwood Studios in Los Angeles for the Death Pixie writing camp, showing how a team builds tracks for a virtual rapper character using Suno.

picks.title: MuLaCover: Flexible Cover Song Generation via Symbolic Tonal Control
picks.rationale: New research: MuLaCover holds melody and chords fixed while a pretrained music language model changes style and instrumentation. That gives explicit control over AI cover and re-arrangement work.
picks.excerpt: A cover-song generation method for pretrained music language models: it explicitly controls tonal content (melody and chords) while reshaping other musical attributes such as style and instrumentation.

picks.title: Suno v. MLC Subpoena Dispute Boils Over as AI Platform Demands Multiple Years of DSP-Specific Streaming Data
picks.rationale: New legal front: Suno's subpoena fight with the Mechanical Licensing Collective, in which Suno demands years of DSP-level streaming data. This is a separate proceeding from the label suits already covered.
picks.excerpt: After months of back and forth, a subpoena dispute has boiled over between Suno and the Mechanical Licensing Collective, with Suno demanding years of DSP-specific streaming data.

picks.title: MQAScore: Fine-Grained Text-Music Alignment Evaluation via Large Audio Language Model
picks.rationale: New research: MQAScore checks each musical concept in a prompt one at a time, so it shows which requested attributes a text-to-music output missed. A single similarity score cannot do that.
picks.excerpt: Instead of one global text-audio similarity score, MQAScore uses a large audio language model to check each atomic musical concept in a prompt, showing which attributes a text-to-music output is missing.
